subject: geography
title: Reading thematic maps and data
objective: Interpret maps that show data rather than just places.

lesson.opening: Thematic maps show a pattern — population, rainfall, income — by encoding a value with color, size, or symbols.

sections.heading: Common map types
sections.body: A choropleth shades whole regions by value. An isoline connects points of equal value, like a contour or isobar. A dot map places one dot per count. Each answers a different question.

sections.heading: Reading the legend
sections.body: Always read the units, the class breaks, and the source. The same data can look dramatic or calm depending on how the breaks are chosen.

sections.heading: A caution
sections.body: Color and scale choices can mislead. A map is an argument about data, not the data itself.

activities.prompt: A map that shades each country by population density is a…
A line connecting points of equal temperature is called…
What should you check first when reading a thematic map?
Why can the same data look very different on two maps?
choices: Different class breaks and color choices

activities.prompt: Describe one way a map can mislead even when the data are correct.
activities.context: Class breaks, color, and projection can all exaggerate or hide a pattern.
